title: HTTP Datagram and Capsule Protocol Foundation Architecture
purpose: Define the RFC 9297 foundation for HTTP/3 Datagram payload encoding, SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM negotiation, H3_DATAGRAM_ERROR registration, and base Capsule Protocol entry parsing.
design_summary: The foundation keeps RFC 9297 byte-level behavior in pure HTTP/3 helper types. `Http3Datagram` encodes and parses Quarter Stream ID followed by payload bytes, enforces the RFC 9297 Quarter Stream ID ceiling, maps malformed DATAGRAM payloads to H3_DATAGRAM_ERROR, and derives associated client-initiated bidirectional request stream IDs. `Http3DatagramSupport` models SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM defaults, 0/1 validation, local/peer send gating, 0-RTT nondecreasing validation, and uncreatable associated stream checks. `Http3Capsule` models Type, Length, Value entries, unknown-capsule skipping by caller policy, malformed truncation handling, and DATAGRAM Capsule type 0x00 payload carriage.
data_and_state_considerations: The slice is allocation-bounded around explicit byte arrays and has no transport side effects. It does not send QUIC DATAGRAM frames, open streams, buffer live capsule streams, or perform CONNECT-UDP/IP routing.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Empty HTTP Datagram payloads after the Quarter Stream ID are legal.
Quarter Stream IDs larger than 2^60-1 fail with H3_DATAGRAM_ERROR.
SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM values other than 0 or 1 fail with H3_SETTINGS_ERROR.
Accepted 0-RTT SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM values must not decrease from the stored value.
Truncated Capsule Type, Length, or Value bytes fail as malformed HTTP messages.
DATAGRAM Capsules use Capsule Type 0x00 and carry HTTP Datagram payload bytes directly after the Capsule Length.
risks: Request support policy, Capsule-Protocol header validation, and intermediary conversion policy are intentionally left for later RFC 9297 slices.
CONNECT-UDP and CONNECT-IP semantics are intentionally left for RFC 9298 and RFC 9484 slices.
This slice does not wire the runtime QUIC DATAGRAM send/receive path into HTTP/3 request dispatch.

supplemental_sections.heading: Implementation Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: The foundation is intentionally reusable by later MASQUE work: RFC 9298 and RFC 9484 can call the HTTP Datagram and Capsule helpers without depending on request handler or proxy runtime state.
